alex: Hey team — escalated customer ticket. Their CI jobs started failing intermittently the past 6h with 403s on object uploads. They say nothing changed in pipeline, but we rolled a policy change overnight reducing SA impersonation token lifetime.

maria: Can you paste the exact error from the job log? 1-2 lines is fine. Also which runner (gitlab/github) and runner version?

alex: From job log: `ERROR: upload failed: POST https://storage.example.com/upload -> 403 Forbidden (Request had insufficient authentication scopes).` Right above: `oauth2 token expires_in=59`. Runner: GitLab shared runner 14.10.

raj: Interesting — `expires_in=59` means impersonated access token lifetime is ~1m. We recently tightened impersonation default to 60s for that org. If runner caches creds across parallel jobs, short TTL can expire mid-upload.

liz: Repro idea: start two parallel jobs that request impersonation token, let one acquire token, then sleep >60s so token expires, then the other job reuses cached credential helper file -> 403.

alex: Customer says some jobs succeed, some fail even within same pipeline. They attached a small snippet: 
```
# job pre-step
gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-bot@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# result
{"access_token":"ya29...","expires_in":59}
```

maria: That `expires_in` number is the smoking gun. If the helper writes token to disk and runner reuses it, a 60s TTL is risky. What are their runner cache settings?

alex: They use default gitlab-runner caching and a shared cache volume. We asked for runner config but haven't got it yet. Customer asked if we can suggest immediate mitigations.

raj: Short-term: increase impersonation lifetime to at least 5m (preferably 1h) for the CI service account. Example: `gcloud iam service-accounts generate-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-bot@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com --lifetime=3600s --scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` (or set in config for your impersonation provider).

liz: Also recommend disabling long-lived credential caching in the runner. For GitLab runner, ensure `auth_helper`/`session_server` isn't reusing files across concurrent jobs, or set per-job workspace isolation.

alex: Customer asked about least-privilege — they only need object write and logs write. Is it safe to bump token TTL and keep tight SA roles?

raj: Yes. TTL is orthogonal to IAM roles. Keep roles scoped (storage.objectAdmin or a custom role limited to bucket). Increasing token lifetime to 1h just reduces refresh frequency, not permissions. But audit and rotate keys as normal.

maria: Also propose a more robust long-term fix: switch to workload identity / OIDC (GitHub Actions native or GitLab OIDC) so each job gets fresh tokens from provider instead of relying on cached impersonation tokens. That avoids runner-level caching issues.

alex: Repro steps we asked customer to run and share back: 
1) `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-bot@PROJECT` twice in a row and note `expires_in`.
2) Start a dummy upload job: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-bot@PROJECT)" -F file=@/dev/null https://storage.example.com/upload` then sleep 90s and re-run the same curl with the previously printed token (to show it fails).

support-bot: [ticket #INC-4391] linked to this thread.

maria: If customer approves, we can temporarily bump org impersonation default via policy and suggest runner config changes. I'll draft an email with command snippets and safe rollback steps.

alex: Perfect. I'll ask them to provide runner config and the two `print-access-token` outputs. Also asked them to confirm which buckets and jobs failed so we can look for correlated logs in our gateway.

raj: One more note — check for proxy or token-exchange layers that might truncate `expires_in` on the way back. We had a case where a sidecar returned scaled-down TTLs causing similar symptoms.

liz: Filed an infra follow-up to add a monitoring alert: if any impersonate call returns expires_in < 300s for CI SAs, fire a pager so we can catch regressions.

alex: Thanks all — I'll update ticket and ping when we get runner config + token outputs. :thumbsup:
